newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli cabinet to take up budget cuts on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Israeli cabinet to take up budget cuts on Tuesday.

text.p: Israel's cabinet will meet on Tuesday at 8:30 p.m. (1730 GMT) to discuss Treasury proposals to cut 800 million shekels ($226 million) from the 1997 budget, the Treasury said on Sunday.
The reductions will include 180 million shekels needed to offset $50 million in U.S. foreign aid Israel has agreed to transfer to Jordan.
The spending cuts have the support of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has been lobbying cabinet ministers in the past week, Treasury sources said.
"The ministers basically accept it. I don't see any major opposition," a Treasury source said.
But the sources said the cuts were not enough to keep this year's deficit to the government's target of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
They said the reductions would have had to reach nearly two billion shekels to contain the deficit, but that the cabinet would never approve such big cuts.
The sources said the smaller reduction was aimed at easing the way for the Treasury to reach its 1998 deficit goal of 2.4 percent of GDP.
